what_was_built: build/facts/build_facts.js: orchestrator and join. `node build_facts.js <sha> <outdir> [--task children] [--skip kinds] [--only kinds] [--keep-export]`. Each task's parent is exported with git archive and the tar is parsed in memory; the working tree is never read. The search is a Node line scan. Round one reads the seed and greps three things: the seed name, the module-path and import spellings (Python dotted, from-import and relative; JS/TS specifiers resolved through the repo aliases), and the route strings in the seed (client /api literals, backend decorators plus the router prefix). The imports seen in the seed are included. Round two opens the top k files and greps their hit definitions, their spellings and their routes. Hits are ranked by an idf-weighted count with type weights: def 3, import 2, mock 1.5, call 1. BM25 is written by hand (k1 1.2, b 0.75). The variants cover one or two rounds, names only or names plus routes, and with or without BM25, plus a BM25-only variant.

Floor DIR: the seed's own directory first, then the same-named capability folder in the other runtimes, then outward by parent directory. Floor CO: built from facts/cache/<parent>/commits.jsonl, which holds ancestor commits only, with same-PR siblings and in-flight PRs already dropped. Files are ranked by confidence, then recency, with DIR order as the tail.

40-configuration TUNE sweep (sweep.js), the same count as arms/common/config.js: one factor at a time around a base. deviations_from_protocol: Tuning labels were re-derived from git for TUNE commits only, by tune_labels.js. For each task it takes the child of the task's parent that changes the seed, then that commit's other existing code/test/migration files, plus the definitions at the parent touched by the diff's old-side hunks. The script exits if it reaches a HELD-OUT commit. sealed/ was never read or listed. These labels may differ from the sealed reference; score.js accepts any labels file of the same shape, so the choice can be re-checked on the sealed TUNE file.
The commit export is parsed in memory from git archive output instead of being extracted under build/tmp. Nothing is written, so there is nothing to delete.
Enclosing definitions (symbol names and line ranges) come from the shared facts node table. No edges are used, so search answers name symbols exactly as the other arms do.
Round one includes the seed's own in-repo imports, which a person reading the seed sees. The sweep has an ablation (seedImports=off) that costs about 0.007 R8k.
Round two greps at most 3 hit definitions per opened file (namesPerFile 3). A term with more than 300 grep lines is dropped as too generic, as a person would refine or abandon it.

Under the shared packer rule, symbol granularity cannot carry file-only units. An import hit is therefore followed to the definitions that use the imported names, and that step is costed as a grep. Fill at symbol granularity uses the fill files' top-level definitions.

Selection rule: the highest R8k among the 40 search configs, then the lowest complexity within one SE. Complexity counts rounds, routes, BM25, fill, proximity, seed imports and symbol granularity. The selection used T1 TUNE only. Nothing was run on HELD-OUT. T3, T4 and T5 are entirely HELD-OUT and were not run.

Tuned on TUNE only: rounds (1, 2); terms (names only, names plus routes); BM25 (off, on, only); DIR fill (on, off); round-two k (3, 5, 8); decay (0.25, 0.5, 1); proximity prior (0, 0.5, 1.5); type weights (typed, flat, def-heavy); null-seed name cap (0, 8, 16); seed imports (on, off); generic cap (100, 300, 1000); granularity (file, symbol); form (paths, signature, range, snippet). The TQ scripts are generic per question kind and were not tuned against any answer. During debugging I looked at the frozen commit's text for two TQ terms (ops_proxy_token, 'current status'). The fixes I then made are generic: the screen import closure is limited to the transport layer plus the screen's own feature folder; direct callers are limited to client code; the route grep broadens to the last literal segment when nothing is found.
problems: The primary metric degenerates at file granularity. Paths and range forms list every code/test/migration file at the parent in about 2.5k to 3.3k tokens. File recall at 8k is therefore 1.000 for every arm that pads with a tail (both floors and every fill config), and the combined recall there is about 0.42 for everyone. Recall at 8k only discriminates in signature or snippet form, at symbol granularity, or if padding is ruled out. The orchestrator should decide this before HELD-OUT.

On TUNE, plain search does not beat plain co-change. CO is 0.752 against the frozen search's 0.735 at 8k. Search beats DIR by only +0.017 (SE 0.007). Search's MRR is higher (0.535 vs CO 0.486), so it puts a relevant file first more often, but co-change covers more. armAudit.verdict:
The relational and reference arms are sound. Their outputs match on 7,040 random configurations with 0 mismatches. PPR and the budget walk match hand-computed answers. Query plans use the indexes. The tokenizer and packer are shared, deterministic and respect the budget. No arm reads sealed/, a held-out commit or the task commit when it answers. The held-out lock refuses every case tested.

The harness is not ready to score yet, for three reasons:
(1) The default "locate" rule saturates in paths and range forms. Listing every file scores 0.94 recall in about 2.4k tokens, so the primary metric stops telling arms apart.
(2) There are two scorers. On the same answers, common/score.js and search/score.js differ by +0.035 recall at 8k in signature form, and by +0.48 in paths form.
(3) Padding decides the primary metric. The search arm pads with the same-directory floor (DIR). Without that padding it scores 0.333 at 8k; with it, 0.734, while DIR alone scores 0.719 and co-change alone 0.750. The relational arm and any graph arm have no padding option and leave the budget unused on 66% of base answers.

Two leakage channels are latent rather than active:
- every facts meta.json names the task commit SHA;
- arms/search/tune_labels.jsonl rebuilds 99.7% of the sealed TUNE reference files inside the arms folder, and the search configuration was selected on it.

The search baseline is not a strawman. On five TUNE tasks my own grep scored 0.231 at 8k against the script's 0.181, with no padding. With the same padding both scored 0.776. But it is only DIR plus about 0.015.

To be tuned as hard as the relational arm, a graph arm needs:
- an async rank() in the harness;
- an equivalence rule that tolerates native PPR and path-order differences;
- its own 40-configuration list around its own base;
- the same padding option and one scorer for every arm.

checks.what: 1. Leakage: static grep of arms, facts and harness code
checks.result: pass at query time; two latent channels
checks.detail: No reference to sealed/ in any query path. git calls: search uses git archive <parent> only. Relational and reference start no child process. Latent channel 1: arms/search/tune_labels.js runs git diff from each parent to its task commit. Its output, arms/search/tune_labels.jsonl, reproduces 4,958/4,973 sealed TUNE reference files and 5,320/6,764 definitions, and sits in the arms folder. Latent channel 2: facts/cache/<parent>/meta.json switches.task holds the task commit SHA for 53/53 TUNE parents, and every arm loads meta.json. Only extractor_version is used today. The co-change extractor reads post-parent history (task PR ids, later merges) but only to drop ancestor commits, as the protocol requires.

checks.what: 1. Leakage: re-run with file and process access logged
checks.detail: Ran relational and reference 'base' on 628 TUNE tasks, and search with 40 configs + 8 floors on 18 tasks, under audit/arms/accesslog.js. 0 sealed paths, 0 held-out SHAs, 0 non-parent commit SHAs (the remaining 40-hex strings are srcstore content hashes). Facts files read: meta, nodes, edges, commits. The 3 commits.jsonl entries checked for one parent are all ancestors. Logs and analysis: audit/arms/leak/.

checks.what: 2. Held-out discipline
checks.detail: common/run.js exits 2 before reading tasks.jsonl in all four cases: no flag; --allow-heldout without hash; wrong hash; correct hash ba68ab71ebbff9b2 never frozen. search/run.js exits 2 without --allow-heldout but has no frozen-hash check. results/frozen/ does not exist. No result file or record has split heldout. 54 SQLite stores = 53 TUNE parents + 1 bench. The only held-out-parent artefact is srcstore/trees/a31924a.json (the frozen commit, also T5's parent), written by bench/TQ, not by a task run.

checks.what: 3. Equivalence relational vs reference
checks.detail: Random configurations, almost none in the 40-config sweep: random class subsets incl. membership/docs/capability, hops 1-6/null, budgets, indeg k 2-25, transport, PPR restart 0.1-0.7 and co-change weight 0-5, 2-3-part hybrids, all forms and granularities, closure/CTE/level-wise paths. 960 comparisons on 32 tasks (seed 7) + 6,080 on 152 tasks across all 53 TUNE parents (seed 2026): 0 mismatches in ranked lists and packed answers. Re-running 'base' reproduced the stored sweep byte-for-byte (1,256 answers, ms excluded). One defect found: a budget config with about 9 classes at 2-3 crashes the reference arm (Set maximum size exceeded); later runs capped the state space at 2,000.

checks.what: 4. Relational design: indexes and query plans
checks.detail: Re-derived EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN on a cached store. k-hop CTE, reach DAG and budget CTE use edge PRIMARY KEY (src=?) and COVERING INDEX edge_rev (dst=?). sqlite_stat1 present (ANALYZE ran). Full scans only in per-configuration cached builds (hub sets, PPR transitions). The class mask is filtered after the index probe (cid not in the key): fine at this degree.

checks.what: 4. Recursion semantics and depth cap
checks.detail: k-hop CTE uses UNION over (node, depth) with r.d < $H, so a node can be re-expanded once per depth level, bounded by H. Unbounded runs level by level with INSERT OR IGNORE into hop (true visited set). Budget CTE uses UNION over (node, state, depth) and terminates because the state counters only grow. The closure table is bounded at K=3 and the base mask, and is used only when it applies.

checks.what: 4. Personalised PageRank against hand computation
checks.detail: 4-node graph (a->b, a->c, b->c, c->d; seed a; restart 0.3; d dangles to the seed). Hand values b 0.148211, c 0.251959, d 0.176371. Relational result: max abs error 1.25e-9, same order c,d,b, reference identical. Second case (direction both, co-change arc x3, restart 0.15) against an exact Gaussian solve: max abs error 1.46e-8, order d,c,b,e identical.

checks.what: 4. Metapath (per-class budget) against a hand walk
checks.detail: Budget imports<=1, calls<=2 on an 8-node toy graph. Reach, hops and via paths equal the hand walk: a1 calls, b1 imports, c2 calls>calls, e2 calls>imports, f3 calls>calls>imports; g and h unreached. Caveat: the budget is a multiset of counts per CLASS, not per edge type and not an ordered type sequence. An ordered metapath (e.g. calls then imports) cannot be expressed in config.js. The state space grows exponentially with the number of classes.

checks.what: 4. Section 6 algorithms present
checks.detail: Present: hops 1-6 and unbounded; per-class budgets; three directions; edge classes added one at a time; bfs, degnorm, PPR 0.15/0.30/0.50, co-change weight 0.5/1/3, co-change rank, FTS5 text, two hybrids; indeg 5/10/15 and transport hubs; file and symbol granularity; 4 forms; 4 budgets. Missing from the sweep: symbol+paths form, symbol+signature-only variants beyond 'gran=symbol', any interaction (one-factor-at-a-time around a base fixed before any data), the optional global cap in budget mode, and the experimental response-field class. The global PageRank column is stored but no ranking uses it.

checks.what: 5. Search baseline quality (sealed TUNE T1, 65 commits)
checks.result: reasonable search, but it is the DIR floor plus padding
checks.detail: R8k common-locate / search-scorer: frozen 'rounds=1 names-only' 0.734/0.698; best 'prox=1.5' 0.744/0.708; DIR floor 0.719/0.683; CO floor 0.750/0.713; frozen without DIR fill 0.333/0.319; 'nofill' 0.489. The frozen choice holds on sealed TUNE: it is within one SE of the best under both scorers. The proxy labels inflated the reported R8k (0.735 under the search scorer vs 0.698 on sealed). Co-change, which a careful person also checks with git log, is a floor and not part of the arm.

checks.what: 5. Beat the search by hand on five TUNE tasks
checks.detail: Tasks T1-0051, T1-0086, T1-0103, T1-0132, T1-0318. Lists written from 4-8 greps each before opening the references (audit/arms/manual_lists.json). Unpadded R8k: hand 0.231 vs scripted 0.181. With the same DIR fill: 0.776 vs 0.776 at 8k, 0.33 vs 0.24 at 2k, 0.51 vs 0.39 at 4k. Most misses were files the commit changed with no code link to the seed: T1-0318 (conftest seed, 14 attendance/web reference files); T1-0103 (api.ts seed, reference = App.tsx only). No search or graph method reaches these files; only proximity padding does.

checks.what: 6. Tokenizer and packer
checks.detail: One tokenizer and one packer (common/) used by search (pack.js adapter), relational and reference; search's tokens-read ledger uses the same tokenizer. Headers are counted: a path line costs 12 tokens; the footer costs 7-8 and is counted in used. 21,928 stored answers (relational, reference, search incl. paths/snippet/symbol forms): 0 over budget, 0 where used fails to recompute from items + cut + footer. Re-runs are byte-identical. The cut item is truncated at atomic tokenizer segments. Minor: a truncated path in paths/range form still counts as a full hit in the common scorer. The footer exceeds its 8-token reserve only above 999,999 units.

checks.what: 7. Scorer consistency (affects every arm)
checks.detail: Two scorers. common/score.js 'locate' credits every definition of a listed file in paths/range form and any shown signature line inside a definition's range. search/score.js credits a definition only by name, or by its start line being shown. Same search answers, R8k: signature 0.734 vs 0.698; paths 0.941 vs 0.459. Under 'locate', DIR in paths form reaches 0.925 at 2k. Every arm can reach 0.94 by listing all files, so selecting by the primary metric would pick paths/range form for every arm. 5.3% of reference definitions are in the seed's own file and no file-granularity answer can show them. That caps everyone equally.

checks.what: 7. What a graph arm needs and harness handicaps
checks.detail: (a) common/arms.js openArm hard-codes relational/reference. run.js and sweep.js call arm.rank() synchronously, but graph-engine drivers are async, so the harness must await. (b) Equivalence is byte-identical over rounded scores, via paths chosen by minimum (u id, kind id), and PPR with fixed 40 iterations and dangling mass returned to the seeds. Native engine PageRank uses tolerance stopping and different dangling handling, so native algorithms will not match bitwise; the protocol needs a stated rank-equivalence tolerance or the graph arm must re-implement these semantics. (c) The 40-config list is one-factor-at-a-time around a base fixed by the relational builder (PPR r0.30, hops 2). The graph arm should get its own 40 around its own base, scored and selected by the grader with the same scorer and sealed TUNE references, as should relational and search. (d) The via explanation is never shown to the model or scored, so the graph's explanation paths carry no measurable value in this harness. Communities and ordered metapaths have no config slot. (e) Latency: SQLite is in-process; a server engine adds IPC, so use an embedded engine or report IPC separately. One store per commit means 128 loads. (f) Padding: give every arm the same optional DIR/CO tail, or compare recall at equal tokens; otherwise unpadded graph answers (relational base median 5,853 tokens at 8k, 66% fully under budget) are compared with search answers padded to about 7,926 tokens. (g) There is no shared TQ scorer and no lookups-to-80% measure for single-query arms.

defects.what: In paths and range forms at file granularity, a listed file counts as showing every reference definition in it. Listing every file then reaches 0.925 recall at 2k and 0.941 at 8k in about 2.4k tokens (DIR floor, form=paths, sealed TUNE T1). Choosing configurations by the primary metric would therefore pick paths/range plus padding for every arm and tie them all.
defects.fix: Make 'content' the primary rule: paths/range credit files only, never definitions. Or drop paths/range from the primary metric and report them under file recall only. Freeze the rule before any selection.

defects.what: The same answers get different recall from the two scorers. Signature form at 8k: 0.734 (common) vs 0.698 (search). Paths form: 0.941 vs 0.459. Definitions are matched by line overlap in one and by name or start line in the other. MRR is item-level in one and file-level in the other. The search arm's published numbers come from its own scorer and proxy labels.
defects.fix: Score every arm with one scorer (common/score.js with the fixed rule) against sealed TUNE references, run by the grader. Retire search/score.js or make it a wrapper around common/score.js.

defects.where: arms/search/arm.js fill (DIR tail); common harness has no equivalent
defects.what: The search arm pads every answer with the directory/capability floor: frozen R8k 0.734 with padding, 0.333 without, DIR floor alone 0.719. Relational and graph answers stop at their reach set: relational base uses a median 5,853 of 8,000 tokens and 66% of answers end under 8k. Recall at 8k then rewards padding, not retrieval, and the win rule's token clause pulls the other way.
defects.fix: Make padding a shared, arm-independent packer option (the same DIR/CO tail) that every arm may switch on, counted in the same configuration budget. Also report recall at matched tokens and the unpadded curve.

defects.what: The search builder rebuilt the TUNE references from the task commits (git diff parent..child). The result reproduces 99.7% of sealed reference files and 79% of definitions and is stored inside arms/. The search configuration was self-selected on it, while the relational arm left selection to the grader. Tuning procedures differ between arms, and another arm builder can read the file.
defects.fix: Move or delete tune_labels.jsonl out of arms/. Let the grader select every arm's configuration with the same sealed TUNE references and scorer. Record the deviation.

defects.where: facts/cache/<parent>/meta.json (switches.task, git stats); loaded by arms/common/facts.js
defects.what: Every facts meta.json the arms load names the task commit SHA (53/53 TUNE parents). No arm uses it today, but any arm, including a future graph arm, could git show the answer.
defects.fix: Strip switches.task and task_children/task_prs from the meta.json the arms read, or keep them in a sealed side file.

defects.what: Search refuses held-out without --allow-heldout but does not require a frozen configuration hash, unlike common/run.js.
defects.fix: Route the search arm through common/harness.js checkSplit (flag + matching frozen hash + results/frozen file).

defects.where: arms/reference/ref.js budget mode (and the budget state machine in general)
defects.what: The budget state space is the product of (b_c+1) over classes per node. With about 9 classes at budget 2-3 the reference arm crashes with 'Set maximum size exceeded' while the SQL CTE keeps running. The sweep's B1/B2 (768 and 1,944 states per node) are already the slowest queries (p95 680-722 ms).
defects.fix: Cap the state space (reject or warn above a limit), or restrict budgets to a few classes. If true metapaths are wanted, add an ordered metapath mode (a sequence of edge types), which grows linearly.

defects.where: arms/common/config.js SWEEP and the protocol's 'metapath' wording
defects.what: 'Budget per edge type (metapaths)' is implemented per CLASS as a multiset count, not per edge type or as an ordered type sequence. The 40 configurations vary one factor at a time around a base fixed before any data (PPR r0.30, hops 2), so interactions such as unbounded PPR with hub cuts are never tried.
defects.fix: State the definition in the protocol record. Give each arm its own 40-configuration list around its own base under the same rules. Consider a second-stage sweep on TUNE around the best first-stage point, the same for every arm.

defects.where: arms/common/arms.js openArm, run.js and sweep.js (synchronous rank())
defects.what: The harness calls arm.rank() synchronously and only knows relational/reference. A graph-engine driver is asynchronous, so a graph arm cannot plug in without harness changes. ms timing is in-process for SQLite but would include IPC for a server engine.
defects.fix: Make rank() awaitable in run.js and sweep.js, register the graph arm in openArm, and time query execution separately from client IPC.

defects.where: Cross-check rule (protocol 5d) as implemented in sweep.js
defects.what: Identity is checked byte-for-byte over 12-decimal scores, via paths chosen by minimum (u id, kind id), and PPR with fixed 40 iterations and dangling mass returned to the seeds. A graph engine's native PageRank and path functions will not reproduce these bitwise, so a graph arm would fail the cross-check for reasons unrelated to answer quality.
defects.fix: Define equivalence as an identical reach set plus an identical rank order wherever score gaps exceed a stated tolerance (e.g. 1e-9), with via compared as a set of valid shortest paths. Or require the graph arm to state where its native algorithm departs from this specification.

defects.where: arms/common/packer.js + score.js (cut item in paths/range form)
defects.what: When the cut lands in a paths or range item, the truncated path text still counts as a full hit for that file.
defects.fix: Count a cut paths/range item only if the whole path line fits.
